tools.name: Figma

Outline text on = text becomes paths (accurate, not editable); Include id attribute keeps layer names as ids. Plugin API can export nodes as SVG programmatically.

Exact current prices vary between third-party sources and could not be checked on figma.com (host blocked in this session). Known SVG export quirks (secondary sources): layer-name-derived ids can contain unsafe characters; text outlining changes the file size and loses editability; effects such as blurs/blend modes/some gradients may not round-trip. Treat Figma export as a starting point and run it through SVGO. Not verified on the official help centre.

tools.name: ImageMagick
tools.summary: Batch rasterising SVG to PNG/JPG/WebP and general bitmap post-processing from the CLI (`magick in.svg out.png`); not an SVG editor.
tools.license: ImageMagick License (permissive, Apache-2.0-like, GPLv3-compatible; no SPDX id in the file I read)
tools.install: brew install imagemagick | apt install imagemagick (CLI is `magick`; IM6 packages on older distros use `convert`)
tools.svg_notes: SVG is decoded by one of three back-ends, picked by how the build was configured: (1) the `svg` delegate in delegates.xml, which shells out to `rsvg-convert` (librsvg), (2) an Inkscape delegate (`svg:decode`, uses `inkscape --export-filename`), or (3) the built-in MSVG/XML renderer (SVG -> MVG). Source builds default to `--with-rsvg=no` (configure.ac), so a self-built binary falls back to MSVG unless librsvg is requested. Run `magick -list format | grep -i svg` and `magick -list delegate` to see what your install uses. Community guidance (forum, secondary) ranks quality Inkscape > RSVG > MSVG; MSVG is weakest (CSS, filters, text).
tools.caveats: Security: ImageMagick has a long CVE history in SVG/MVG/MSL and URL/delegate handling. Never feed it untrusted SVG without a restrictive policy.xml (disable MVG/MSL/URL/HTTPS coders, limit resources). Distro default policy files are 'open' and meant for trusted/sandboxed use. For local dev with your own files this is fine. A policy can block SVG outright (users hit 'not authorized' errors). If you only need SVG -> PNG, resvg or rsvg-convert are more predictable. Current release number NOT verified (a Cygwin announcement from Dec 2025 lists 7.1.2.3).
tools.verification_level: primary for licence and delegate wiring (GitHub raw LICENSE, config/delegates.xml.in, configure.ac); secondary for renderer-quality ranking and policy behaviour

tools.name: Inkscape
tools.summary: Full-featured desktop vector editor with SVG as its native format; also has a CLI (`inkscape --export-type=png ...`) usable as an ImageMagick delegate, path ops, trace bitmap, text-to-path.
tools.license: GPL-2.0-or-later (source; complete binaries are effectively GPL-3.0-or-later per COPYING)
tools.install: brew install --cask inkscape | apt install inkscape | flatpak install org.inkscape.Inkscape
tools.svg_notes: Native Inkscape SVG with sodipodi/inkscape namespaces; save as 'Optimized SVG' or 'Plain SVG' for clean output. CLI export of PNG/PDF/EPS/plain SVG.
tools.caveats: Latest stable tag found on GitLab: INKSCAPE_1_4_4 (2026-05-05); master is 1.5-dev. Inkscape-specific metadata bloats files, so run SVGO or save as Plain SVG before committing.

tools.name: librsvg (rsvg-convert)
tools.summary: GNOME's SVG renderer and its `rsvg-convert` CLI: reliable SVG to PNG/PDF/PS/SVG; the delegate ImageMagick prefers over its internal renderer.
tools.install: brew install librsvg | apt install librsvg2-bin
tools.svg_notes: Targets SVG 1.1 and parts of SVG 2; no scripting and no CSS animation (README). Rust codebase, version 2.63.4 in Cargo.toml on main.
tools.caveats: Static rendering only: animated SVG renders as its first frame. Not all SVG 2/filters features are supported (see its features chapter).

tools.name: Playwright
